H.R. 1501 – Protecting Domestic Mining Act (Rep. Shreve – Natural Resources) (Subject to a Rule)

This bill amends the Fixing America’s Surface Transportation (FAST) Act to codify mining and mineral processing as covered sectors, allowing such projects to be eligible for an alternative permitting system known as FAST-41. These activities are already eligible for FAST-41 through regulation. The bill also prohibits the Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council from finalizing, implementing, or enforcing the Biden Administration proposed rule titled “Revising Scope of the Mining Sector of Projects That Are Eligible for Coverage Under Title 41 of the Fixing America’s Surface Transportation Act.” 

Once again, House Republicans are choosing to prioritize the mining industry over protecting the environment and public health. The FAST-41 permitting process can limit opportunities for public input and judicial review, making it more difficult to obtain temporary restraining orders or preliminary injunctions against mining projects that threaten wildlife and nearby populations. The codification of all mining and mineral processing as covered sectors could also further undermine Tribal sovereignty and even jeopardize culturally significant sites for Tribal communities.

Additionally, by preventing the Biden Administration proposed rule – which is designed to limit mineral projects eligible for FAST-41 to only those involving critical minerals and their supply chains – from ever taking effect, this bill could also restrict future administrations from making necessary modifications to the scope of covered mining projects. Rather than work to shield the public from potentially harmful mining efforts and unforeseen complications, House Republicans would rather permanently benefit the mining industry – at the expense of everyday Americans and the places they call home.

Ranking Member Huffman strongly opposes this bill.

The Rule, which was adopted yesterday, provides for one hour of debate equally divided and controlled by the Chair and Ranking Member of the Committee on Natural Resources or their respective designees.

Suspension (1 bill)

  1. H.J.Res. 1 – Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices (Rep. Biggs (AZ) – Judiciary) – VOTE NO

This proposed constitutional amendment would permanently fix the number of Supreme Court justices at nine, stripping Congress of yet another constitutional authority that is meant to be controlled by the American people's representatives.

H.J.Res. 1 represents the further weakening of Congress under Republican control. This Republican majority – which has already surrendered Congressional war powers, Congressional taxing and tariff powers, and Congressional spending powers to President Trump – would now permanently relinquish the power to set the number of Supreme Court Justices, given to Congress in Article I of the Constitution. 

Over the course of history, Congress has periodically exercised its constitutional authority to pass legislation changing the size, structure, and jurisdiction of the Court and federal judiciary to reflect political, geographic, and demographic changes in the country. Congress has shrunk the size of the Court to as little as five justices and expanded it to as many as ten justices to address the needs of the judiciary at the time. H.J.Res. 1 is not a serious effort to improve our constitutional system or address the challenges everyday Americans are facing. It is yet another attempt by House Republicans to surrender Congress’ constitutional powers and oversight duties over both the President and the Supreme Court.

Right now, the country is facing an affordability crisis caused by decisions made by this administration. Between President Trump’s disastrous tariff regime and war of choice with Iran, inflation remains high and soaring costs for gas, groceries, and more are forcing Americans to stretch every dollar available. House Democrats are ready to work on solutions to these problems, but House Republicans have decided to prioritize a constitutional amendment that does nothing to help their constituents make ends meet.

Ranking Member Raskin strongly opposes this resolution.

H.R. 9436 – Northeast Lobsterman Protection Act of 2026 (Rep. Lawler – Natural Resources) (Subject to a Rule) – VOTE NO

This bill would extend the deadline for implementing new regulations to reduce entanglements of North Atlantic right whales in the American Lobster and Jonah Crab fisheries from 2028 to 2035.

Fisheries in state and federal waters have been required to reduce whale injury and mortality by complying with the Atlantic Large Whale Take Reduction Plan (TRP) – directly addressing the fishing gear and vessel strikes that are leading to the species decline of the right whale. In 2022, the TRP was deemed out of compliance with the Marine Mammal Protection Act and the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) was ordered to update the plan. While Congress implemented a moratorium on these new regulations, granting an extension two years before the moratorium is set to expire is premature in the face of the available science.

House Republicans have presented this bill as a false choice between conservation of the right whale and supporting lobster fisheries. When the original moratorium was enacted, Congress directed NMFS to work with affected states and fisheries on fully voluntary efforts to promote and research innovative gear technologies. Additionally, approximately $20 million has been appropriated for the development of innovative fishing technologies since 2022. Resources are clearly available to support lobster fisheries without risking further population decline of the right whale, but House Republicans are choosing to ignore this reality and instead put a critically endangered species at even greater risk.

Ranking Member Huffman strongly opposes this bill.

The Rule will provide for one hour of debate equally divided and controlled by the Chair and Ranking Member of the Committee on Natural Resources or their respective designees.

H.Res. 1490 – Providing for the condemnation and denouncement of socialism in all its forms (Rep. Crank – House Administration) (Subject to a Rule)

Rather than put forward legislation that would meaningfully make life better for everyday Americans, House Republicans are wasting valuable Floor time to once again bolster President Trump’s efforts to subvert democracy. This resolution calls for the enactment of the SAVE America Act, a piece of legislation that would disenfranchise countless American citizens – including our military, Native Americans, people who have changed their names (including tens of millions of American women), seniors, rural voters, and more – as they try to participate in free and fair American elections. If House Republicans were truly serious about protecting election integrity and the ability of government to serve the people, they would stand up to a president that continuously undermines the democratic process. 

Ranking Member Morelle strongly opposes this resolution.

The Rule will provide for one hour of debate equally divided and controlled by the Chair and Ranking Member of the Committee on House Administration or their respective designees.
